concept.title: Same-Prime Square Plane Transversal Difference Conjecture
concept.concept_description: For any odd prime $p$, let $G = (\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z})^2$ and $H = pG$. The transversal difference number $\delta(G, H)$, which is the minimum size of the difference support $T - T$ over all transversals $T$ for $G/H$, is exactly $(2p - 1)^2$.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any odd prime $p$, let $G = (\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z})^2$ and $H = pG$. The transversal difference number $\delta(G, H)$, which is the minimum size of the difference support $T - T$ over all transversals $T$ for $G/H$, is exactly $(2p - 1)^2$.
concept.lean_guess: Translate the transversal difference problem into an optimization over functions $\mathbb{F}_p^2 \to \mathbb{F}_p^2$ representing transversals, where the difference support decomposes into carry-corrected finite-field derivative images. Apply Kneser's theorem for cross-transversal estimates and analyze polynomial sections to establish that the minimal difference support is achieved by linear sections, yielding the exact $(2p-1)^2$ bound.

concept.title: Poset Realization Size for $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$
concept.concept_description: For any integer $n \ge 3$, the minimum number of elements in a poset $P$ such that its automorphism group $\text{Aut}(P)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ is exactly $2^{n+1} + 2$. This conjecture formalizes the main theorem of the paper.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any integer $n \ge 3$, the minimum number of elements in a poset $P$ such that its automorphism group $\text{Aut}(P)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ is exactly $2^{n+1} + 2$. This conjecture formalizes the main theorem of the paper.
concept.lean_guess: Define the function $\beta(G)$ as the infimum of the cardinalities of posets $P$ with $\text{Aut}(P) \cong G$. The upper bound is established by constructing a poset of size $2^{n+1}+2$ realizing the group, which can be done via a recursive construction adding two minimal elements (as in Proposition 2.2). The lower bound requires showing that any poset realizing this group must have at least $2^{n+1}+2$ elements, utilizing the structural constraints of the group action on the poset.

concept.concept_description: For any connected graph G with an edge partition P of E(G) into t classes, let A be the cycle-class parity matrix over GF(2) constructed from P. The induced quotient labeling ℓ: V(G) → (Z/2Z)^(t − rank(A)) satisfies d_G(u,v) ≥ d_H(ℓ(u), ℓ(v)) for all u,v ∈ V(G), where H is the hypercube Cayley graph on (Z/2Z)^(t − rank(A)). That is, the labeling never stretches distances—it can fail to be isometric only by shortcuts (contracting distances), never by stretching them.

concept.lean_guess: Show that each edge of G maps to an edge of H under the quotient labeling (by construction of the labeling from the edge partition), so every path in G maps to a path of equal or shorter length in H. The key step is proving that the GF(2) quotient construction preserves adjacency: if uv ∈ E(G) and uv lies in partition class i, then ℓ(u) and ℓ(v) differ in exactly the coordinate corresponding to the image of class i in the quotient. Map the rational points back to integer solutions $(n,t)$ and verify that exactly these five solutions exist.
